- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.6) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior peak), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above recent high for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.3) mid-period, model frequently underestimates; adjust upward by 0.5–1.5% to counteract mean reversion bias.
- Model underperforms when sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.3–0.6); use 3-day moving average of history to anchor forecast if sentiment lacks direction.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture late-period momentum; add 1–2% lagged sentiment-weighted adjustment to final 5–7 days.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., +0.7 → -0.2 → +0.6), model overfits short-term noise; apply smoothing filter (e.g., 5-day EWMA) to forecast.
